newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Huan Hsin's IPO to give diversification a lift-off.
newsitem.headline: Huan Hsin's IPO to give diversification a lift-off.

text.p: Huan Hsin Holdings Ltd's initial public offer (IPO) launched on Thursday will give its diversification plans a lift-off, senior officials said.

They said Huan Hsin, which gets most of its revenue from telephone cords, is using a substantial portion of the estimated US$19.7 million proceeds to set up new facilities for plastic injection moulded products.
It is offering 50 million new shares at US$0.42 each for listing on the main board of the Stock Exchange of Singapore.

"We are investing heavily in plasic injection moulding. In 1997, telephone cords would still constitute a substantial portion of our revenue but in coming years, plastic injection will become more important," Hsu Cheng Chien, Huan Hsin's managing director, told a news conference.
In 1996, the company recorded revenues of Singapore $47.3 million, of which 83 percent came from telephone cords and related components. Net profit was S$9.98 million.

The company is allocating US$10.3 million to build new manufacturing facilities in three phases into 1998 in Shanghai, China. Most of the facilities would be for plastic injection moulding activities.
It is also spending US$4.8 million in new machinery for plastic injection moulding which would allow the company to make larger-sized products like computer monitor casings.
In the past, Huan Hsin's plastic injection moulded products were mostly for its own use.
"We hope that eventually telephone cords will make up 50 percent of sales and other products will make up the other 50 percent," Hsu said.
Other products include power cords, computer cables, handset receivers and LAN cables used for computer network, telephone and video equipment.
But the company saw its telephone cord business continuing to grow.
"There is a lot of room (for telephone cord) to grow because the rate of installation in emerging markets of telephones is low," Hsu said.
He added that more people in advanced countries were installing more than one fixed-telephone line in the home and consumers were quick to replace their telephone cords as well.
Huan Hsin supplies telephone cords to Siemens, AT&T, and Northern Telecom, among others.
The company presently has a plant in Malaysia serving the Southeast Asian market and another in Shanghai, focused on Europe, U.S. and Japan customers.
